findings.summary: The window-4 series is encoded in the light tint #7fa9bf and its value labels are drawn in that same tint on white: sampled from the rendered PNG the labels measure 2.52:1 contrast, below the 4.5:1 14 pt text needs and below the 3:1 floor for large text. The second window's numbers (18,953 MB/min, 6,840, 74, 89.3 %, 101.2 %, 12.2 %) therefore read noticeably fainter than the window-3 numbers at 5.54:1, so the like-for-like comparison the figure exists to make is weakest exactly where the two windows are compared. Legible to an ordinary reader, but a lighter-weight encoding of the second arm than the first, and below the contrast floor for a reader with reduced contrast sensitivity.

The figure's alternate text describes the eleven mirror-answered projects as drawn 'in grey', while the rendered bars are the dark blue #2f6f8f and only the two fallback bars are magenta. A reader given the alternate text is told the wrong encoding, and the mirror/fallback distinction is the figure's subject. The picture itself is correct; the description beside it is not.
